featured_reviews.review_text:
1-Star Review: Absolutely Disgusting Experience with Niva Bupa Health Insurance – Conned by Axis Bank and Then Screwed Over by Niva Bupa
I was completely conned into buying a Niva Bupa health insurance policy through my bankers at Axis Bank. They pushed it aggressively like it was the best thing ever, and foolishly, I fell for it. Fast forward to renewal time: I received an intimation email/SMS about 2 months before my policy expiry, so I decided to renew early to avoid any hassle and keep continuous coverage. I paid a hefty ₹47,000 promptly.

Then the nightmare began. I got a call for “phone verification,” which I answered perfectly—no issues there. They assured me I’d receive a link to complete the process, and I’d get my renewed policy. Sure enough, an email arrived with a link. It asked for medical reports, which weren’t handy right then. When I finally got free, gathered the documents, and tried to upload them—the link had expired! Just like that.

Result? My policy was straight-up cancelled. They collected my money, wasted my time, and then killed the policy because their stupid, time-limited link expired on their end. Now they’re refunding the amount (supposedly), but dragging their feet and acting like it’s my fault.

The cherry on top? These clowns are now calling and emailing me, begging me to “renew again” with some fresh nonsense process. Renew again? After this circus? As if I’d trust these incompetent frauds with another rupee! It’s not feasible, not practical, and frankly insulting that they think I’d fall for their garbage twice.

Niva Bupa is a dastardly, cheap, unethical insurance company that relies on mis-selling through banks like Axis, then uses shady, expiring links and poor systems to cancel policies and pocket money temporarily. Their customer service is a joke—zero accountability, endless runaround, and pure frustration.

Even after posting this review, I know they’ll probably send yet another useless link to fill their stupid online form. Well, Niva Bupa and anyone still foolish enough to buy from them—you can all go to hell. Stay far away from this scam of a company. Port out if you’re stuck, complain to IRDAI, or better yet, never touch them in the first place.
Worst decision ever. 0/10. Avoid at all costs!

In 2006, Star Health and Allied Insurance became India's first standalone Health Insurance company. Twenty years later, the launch of Value Plus marks the next chapter, and India's leading publications carried the story.

The Economic Times, covered Star Health's two-decade milestone alongside the launch of Value Plus.

Value Plus is an affordable Health Insurance offering designed to bring wider health protection to young Indians in Tier 2, 3 and 4 cities at nearly 20% lower premiums. It offers high sum-insured covers from ₹7.5 lakh to ₹25 lakh through a curated network of 11,000+ quality hospitals.

20 years in. The next chapter begins now.

"Insurance growth in India is no longer a metro story. The next wave will come from Tier II, Tier III and Tier IV markets.”

In an interview with Shine Jacob from Business Standard, our MD and CEO Anand Roy laid out why retail health penetration in smaller towns is non-negotiable for the country's Insurance for All by 2047 vision.

The first 20 years helped build India's health insurance category. The next 20 will be about taking protection deeper into Bharat.

"GWP up to ₹5,968 crore. Net profit up to ₹111 cr."

That was the headline takeaway in The Economic Times, on Star Health and Allied Insurance's Q4 FY26 results.

The coverage walked through the company's Q4 numbers. Net profit at ₹111 crore, a multi-fold jump from ₹50 lakh in the same quarter last year. Net Premium at ₹5,599 crore, up from ₹4,820 crore YoY. Total income at ₹4,545 crore, up from ₹3,989 crore YoY. And the underwriting loss narrowed sharply to ₹154 crore from ₹275 crore in the year-ago period.

Star Health has launched 32 Arogya Seva Kendras (ASK) under its CSR initiative to strengthen access to community-level primary healthcare across nine states, with the goal of impacting over one million lives.

In partnership with Piramal Swasthya (part of Piramal Foundation), these clinics will provide free primary healthcare services, including:

* MBBS doctor consultations
* Screening for hypertension, diabetes, and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs)
* Laboratory diagnostics and essential medicines
* Health counselling and awareness sessions
* Adult pneumococcal vaccination support, with expertise from Pfizer

With hypertension prevalence ranging from 20–40% and diabetes affecting up to 29% of adults in certain districts, this initiative highlights the urgent need for preventive and accessible primary care to address India’s growing NCD burden.

A meaningful step toward healthcare equity ensuring quality primary care reaches communities early, consistently, and close to home.

Star Health reported strong Q3 FY26 performance, supported by premium growth, disciplined underwriting, and improved operating efficiency.
The quarter reflects sustained focus on profitability, claims excellence, and customer trust.

Sharing a serious and unresolved issue involving both a shipping line and a marine insurer, highlighting significant gaps in accountability and claims handling.
Two containers were shipped together on the same voyage with Interasia Lines Ltd. One container was delivered in sound condition, while the other arrived totally damaged at destination. In accordance with standard procedures, a damage survey was conducted within 24 hours of receipt.
The shipment was insured with TATA AIG Insurance under ICC (A) – All Risks cover, including War Risk policy. A marine insurance claim was duly lodged (Claim No. 4300160663A) with all documents that were available and requested at the time. The last communication from TATA AIG was on 02/06/2025, and the claim remains unsettled.
Despite:
ICC (A) All Risks coverage,
Timely damage survey, and
Clear evidence of selective damage (one container intact, one totally damaged),
Interasia Lines Ltd. has declined responsibility for the cargo damage, and TATA AIG Insurance has failed to bring the claim to a fair and timely conclusion.
For exporters and businesses, marine insurance and reliable shipping are meant to provide protection—not prolonged uncertainty. This experience raises serious concerns about post-shipment accountability, claims efficiency, and customer commitment.
This is shared in the interest of awareness and accountability, with the expectation that both parties act responsibly and resolve genuine cargo damage claims.
